answer: An agent economy resists sybils by making every identity carry a bonded cost it cannot recycle. Before attesting, a node must lock a stake derived from a unique device key; peers keep an atlas mapping each pubkey to one bonded seat, so spawning a thousand ghost agents means posting a thousand real, slashable deposits. Collusion is priced: when a cluster of fresh identities all attest the same block, the shared funding gets flagged and the bond burns, so an attacker pays more than any reward the forge can mint. A cloned ocean of keys becomes a losing trade, and honest agents stay cheap to run.
